The glyfp package provides one interface for structural fingerprints and
pretrained glycan representations. Inputs can be glyrepr structure vectors or
text supported by glyparse. Both encoding functions return only a list of vectors.

## Choose a method

| Method | Coordinates | What fitting does |
|---|---|---|
| `substructure_binary` (default) | Presence/absence of connected residue motifs | Learns a motif dictionary from the supplied batch |
| `substructure_count` | Number of overlapping motif occurrences | Learns the same motif dictionary |
| `sweetnet` | 128 pretrained latent features | Binds and validates a fixed model, vocabulary and preprocessing |

The sections below use the same three functions: `glycan_fingerprint()`,
`fit_fingerprint()`, and `transform_fingerprint()`.

## Substructure fingerprints

```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>")
```

```{r}
library(glyfp)
a <- c("Galb3Galb3Galb-", "Galb-")
b <- c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", NA_character_)
```

`glycan_fingerprint()` fits on the current batch and returns only a list of
vectors. For joint comparison combine the batches before fitting:

```{r}
all_fp <- glycan_fingerprint(c(a, b), "substructure_count")
lengths(all_fp)
```

Independent calls do not define a shared space, even at equal lengths:

```{r}
glycan_fingerprint("Gal(b1-")
glycan_fingerprint("Man(a1-")
```

For repeated batches, retain one encoder. In model evaluation, fit it using
training data only, then transform held-out data.

```{r}
encoder <- fit_fingerprint(a, "substructure_count", max_size=2)
fp_a <- transform_fingerprint(a, encoder)
fp_b <- transform_fingerprint(b, encoder)
stopifnot(identical(names(fp_a[[1]]), names(fp_b[[1]])))
stopifnot(all(is.na(fp_b[[2]])))
```

Text parsing is delegated to glyparse; structure objects produce the same values.

```{r}
objects <- glyparse::auto_parse(a)
stopifnot(identical(transform_fingerprint(objects, encoder), fp_a))
```

Overlap is counted: the Gal-Gal motif occurs twice in the chain of three Gal
residues. Branch permutations of a single occurrence do not multiply its count.

```{r}
fp_a[[1]]
symmetric <- "Gal(b1-?)[Gal(b1-?)]GlcNAc(b1-"
glycan_fingerprint(symmetric, "substructure_count")
```

Unknown canonical motifs never append columns. Known generic or ambiguous motifs
can still match more specific input under glymotif's strict semantics.

```{r}
generic <- fit_fingerprint("Hex(?1-", "substructure_count")
transform_fingerprint("Gal(b1-", generic)
```

Use `unknown="warn"` or `unknown="error"` while fitting to detect novel canonical
motifs at transformation. Missing values propagate unless `na_action="error"`.
An encoder fitted on empty/all-NA input has no features, so a length-zero vector
cannot carry missingness; keep the original missing-value mask in that case.

```{r}
empty <- fit_fingerprint(character())
transform_fingerprint(c("Gal(b1-", NA_character_), empty)
```

The encoder can be serialized without graph pointers. Preserve the recorded
versions of glyrepr, glymotif and glyparse when reusing it in another session.

```{r}
path <- tempfile(fileext=".rds")
saveRDS(encoder, path)
stopifnot(identical(transform_fingerprint(a, readRDS(path)), fp_a))
unlink(path)
```

## Pretrained SweetNet embeddings

SweetNet is a graph neural network introduced by
[Burkholz, Quackenbush and Bojar (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2021.109251).
The optional `sweetnet` method runs entirely in R with torch. Binary/count
methods do not load torch or require its runtime.

### Setup and first use

Install the optional R packages and runtime once:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("torch", "digest", "zip"))
torch::install_torch()
```

Then call the same fingerprint API. **No checkpoint environment variable or
manual weight download is required.** The first call downloads the official
SweetNet v2 weights (about 3.82 MB), verifies their SHA-256, and saves them in
your user cache. Later calls reuse the verified file.

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Maintainer-only switch: documentation builds normally run without model downloads.
run_sweetnet <- identical(Sys.getenv("GLYFP_RUN_MODEL_EXAMPLES"), "true")
```

```{r, eval=run_sweetnet}
fp <- glycan_fingerprint(c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc", "GlcNAc"), "sweetnet")
lengths(fp)
```

The default cache location is `tools::R_user_dir("glyfp", "cache")`. Use
`cache_dir` when a different location is needed. No network request occurs when
loading glyfp or using the structural methods. The package does not install the
torch runtime automatically.

### Choose a checkpoint

| `checkpoint` | Model | Representation |
|---|---|---|
| `"sweetnet-v2"` (default) | Current glycowork species model | Residual graph layers with BatchNorm; mean and max pooling |
| `"sweetnet-v1"` | Legacy glycowork 1.9.0 species model | Three graph layers; mean pooling |
| A local `.pt` path | Either of the two official models, identified by hash | Uses the corresponding architecture |

Both models produce 128 learned coordinates. **v1 and v2 define different
coordinate spaces and must not be mixed**, despite sharing vector lengths and
coordinate names. The v2 default follows the current upstream pretrained model;
it does not imply better accuracy for every downstream task.

```{r, eval=run_sweetnet}
a <- c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc", "GlcNAc", NA_character_)
b <- "Man(a1-3)[Man(a1-6)]Man"
encoder <- fit_fingerprint(a, "sweetnet", checkpoint = "sweetnet-v2")
fp_a <- transform_fingerprint(a, encoder)
fp_b <- transform_fingerprint(b, encoder)
stopifnot(all(lengths(fp_a) == 128L), all(is.na(fp_a[[3]])))
stopifnot(identical(names(fp_a[[1]]), names(fp_b[[1]])))
encoder$params$model$model

legacy <- fit_fingerprint(a, "sweetnet", checkpoint = "sweetnet-v1")
stopifnot(!identical(encoder$params$model, legacy$params$model))
```

Fitting binds the fixed model, vocabulary and preprocessing; it does not train or
update weights. Empty/all-NA fitting still defines 128 coordinates. Missing
inputs yield 128 `NA_real_` values unless `na_action = "error"`.

### Offline use and local files

After the first download, `download = FALSE` requires the cached checkpoint and
prevents network access. The encoder preserves that policy for future transforms.

```{r, eval=run_sweetnet}
offline <- fit_fingerprint(a, "sweetnet", download = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(transform_fingerprint(a, offline), fp_a))
```

Alternatively, pass a verified local file. Its contents determine which model is
loaded, regardless of its filename. It is never copied into the cache, replaced,
or downloaded. Arbitrary `.pt` models and altered weights are rejected.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
encoder <- fit_fingerprint(
  a, "sweetnet", checkpoint = "/path/to/glycowork_sweetnet_species_v2.pt",
  download = FALSE
)
```

Downloads go to a temporary file in the cache directory. Only a complete file
matching the fixed SHA-256 is renamed into place. A failed download leaves no
partial checkpoint for a later call to mistake for a valid model. A corrupt
existing cache entry produces an error naming the file: remove that file to
allow a fresh download, or supply a verified local path. Offline cache misses
produce an explicit error and make no network request.

The pinned official artifacts are:

- [SweetNet v2](https://huggingface.co/DBojar/glycowork_models/blob/52187c054b9c988ddb2a5a5af9ee64b51004fd1e/glycowork_sweetnet_species_v2.pt),
  SHA-256 `bc3d901e4284554c1a245b8e6b7e291a5631c8932ca9c27eb8668b6d4424a146`.
- [Legacy SweetNet](https://huggingface.co/DBojar/glycowork_models/blob/0a3981df888532e52b4c2d910bfb56b5a45ad955/glycowork_sweetnet_species.pt),
  SHA-256 `4ee19fc0593db0562c16585b556050694144816754750ebfe1876ed21ba0f4be`.

The authors' model repository is public and MIT licensed. The fixed revision and
hash prevent an upstream replacement from silently changing an encoder's model.

### Supported chemistry

Text parsing is delegated to glyparse; equivalent glyrepr objects use the same
graph construction. An unknown reducing-end annotation at the residue's normal
inferred carbon position, such as `(?1-` for GlcNAc or `(?2-` for Neu5Ac, is omitted
from the model graph. Explicit alpha/beta half-linkages, other reducing-end
positions and ambiguous internal linkages are rejected so specified chemistry
is not silently discarded. Floating parts/substituents and alditols remain
unsupported.

Every residue/substituent/linkage token must be in the fixed pretrained
vocabulary. `unknown = "error"` is the only supported SweetNet policy; tokens
are never assigned untrained representations. `max_size` applies only to the
structural methods.

### Reproducibility and persistence

The encoder records model version, official source revision, weight and
vocabulary hashes, R implementation hashes, package versions, readout, CPU device
and batch size. Every transform validates these records, including empty input.
Use `saveRDS()` and `readRDS()` to retain the encoder, and keep it with any exported
vectors. Local paths must remain accessible. Named models can be downloaded
again after cache removal only when the encoder's download policy permits it.

Both readouts are `bn2(lin2(...))`, before the final activation, dropout and
classifier. Evaluation uses CPU float32, frozen normalization, no gradients or
dropout, and one graph at a time. Caller thread settings and the native backend's
R RNG state are preserved. Runtime binary and hardware identity are not fully
recorded, so comparisons across environments should allow floating-point
tolerance. Model upgrades require refitting and recomputing all compared batches.

Ordinary tests mock network calls. Real pretrained integration tests use local
files specified by developer-only `GLYFP_TEST_CHECKPOINT` (v1) and
`GLYFP_TEST_V2_CHECKPOINT` (v2), comparing all 128 coordinates with independent
upstream reference values at maximum absolute error below `1e-5`.
